claims.text: As-deposited NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 coatings have high residual stresses.
As-deposited NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 coatings have a disordered or unoptimized dislocation and grain-boundary network.
Post-deposition annealing reduces residual stresses in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 coatings.
Post-deposition annealing reorganizes or optimizes the coating's dislocation network.
Post-deposition annealing can tailor the grain-boundary network of a nanocrystalline HEA coating.
Dislocation density is relevant to deformation of NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 between 673 K and 873 K.
Reduced residual stress and an optimized defect network enhance the coating's ability to absorb and distribute wear-induced deformation.
The annealing-induced microstructure delays crack initiation during high-temperature sliding contact.
The annealing-induced microstructure delays crack propagation during high-temperature sliding contact.
Annealed NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 coatings will have lower wear rates than as-deposited controls.
Annealed NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 coatings will have lower friction coefficients than as-deposited controls.
As-deposited controls will form more cracks than annealed coatings under otherwise similar wear tests.
The proposed mechanism should operate in an inert atmosphere from 673 K to 873 K.
The NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy retains yield strength above 800 MPa from 673 K to 873 K.
Annealed coatings can retain a modified defect network without significant secondary-phase formation.
Oxidation or phase transformations could interfere with the proposed annealing-mediated wear mechanism.

contradictions.description: The boundary treats unintended oxidation or phase transformation as interference that places the test outside the intended mechanism, whereas the falsification rule treats unintended secondary phases as directly falsifying the hypothesis. A confounded or failed annealing treatment does not decisively test the proposed stress/defect-mediated mechanism.
